title: Response Shape Guardian + Canary Alerting for Config & Model Changes
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: Build a deploy-time and runtime gating service ('Response Shape Guardian') that detects meaningful changes to API responses' shape and content after model or config changes, and surfaces automated canary alerts or rollbacks. Scope covers: per-route response shape baselines, field-presence & type histograms, categorical value drift for enumerated fields, sample-weighted impact scoring, and an automated canary policy that ties alerts to a specific model/config diff (git commit + model version).
motivation: We have seen subtle regressions where models start omitting or changing types for certain response fields after config tweaks or model swaps. Current detection relies on ad-hoc eval runs; we need an always-on, low-latency detector integrated into rollout pipelines so that regressions are caught before affecting customer traffic at scale.
acceptance_criteria: A daemon (shape-guardian) runs a canary for every rollout and computes a response-shape delta against the stored baseline for that route
Field-level signals produced: presence_rate, type_coherence_score, enum_distribution_shift, example_failure_rate
Automated alert if weighted aggregate score exceeds configured threshold for the canary window
Rollout integration: when a canary triggers, system can optionally pause rollout and flip to fallback model/version
Dashboards showing historical field churn and per-release diff links
A runbook with triage steps and GitHub PR/Confluence links in alerts
proposal_summary: Implement a lightweight microservice that subscribes to canary sample streams and performs per-field analytics. Use rolling-window baselines (7d) for presence/type distributions and compute a normalized 'shape delta' score. Combine this with sample-weighted severity (customers + frequency) and a config-diff tagger so alerts reference the exact model/config commit. Provide a scoring policy that is conservative by default and can be tuned per-route.
implementation_notes: Leverage existing eval harness at tools/evals/canary-harness for sample orchestration
Telemetry emitted as metric series: rg.presence_rate, rg.type_coherence, rg.enum_jsd, rg.shape_delta
Persist per-route baselines in time-series store (Prometheus + long-term snapshot S3 for weekly baselines)
Canary window configurable: default 1h for high-traffic routes, 4h for low-traffic
Decision pipeline: compute z-score per-field -> cap and combine -> apply sample-weighted multiplier -> threshold check
Integrate with rollout controller to support automatic pause & rollback hook
Expose a lightweight REST debug endpoint for on-call to pull sample diffs quickly
implementation_tasks: Schema-free sample normalizer to extract candidate fields from JSON responses
Field metrics collector and aggregator job
Shape delta scoring engine with config-diff tagging
Rollout controller integration and pause/rollback hook
Alerting rules and playbook links in PagerDuty notification
Dashboards + per-release diff view in Console
Unit + integration tests for edge cases (absent fields, null buckets, type flips)
risks: False positives for routes with intentionally heterogenous outputs
Storage cost for retaining sample snapshots long enough to build baselines
Latency impact if canary sampling is synchronous; will use async streams
Tuning thresholds per-route will require ops work and initial noise
